newsitem.title: UK: BSkyB, Carlton, Granada up on digital hopes.
newsitem.headline: BSkyB, Carlton, Granada up on digital hopes.

text.p: Shares in BSkyB Plc, Carlton Communications Plc and Granada Group Plc all rose in a falling market on Monday on hopes about the future of the consortium's digital television venture, traders said.
Shares in BSkyB were up 9p at 608 by 1010 GMT, while Carlton was up 17-1/2p to 576 and Granada 6-1/2p higher at 903-1/2.
"Sentiment is still good after the announcement on Friday," one trader said. "There's good buying in all three stocks."
The three broadcasters teamed up on Friday to form British Digital Broadcasting, a venture under which they hoped to offer viewers 15 subscription channels.

"It's a master coup for BSkyB," said Dennis Exton, media analyst at Nikko Europe. "It's a low-risk path to long-term earnings." But he said the future profitability of Carlton and Granada was uncertain.
"Their traditional earnings from analogue television are threatened and there is a question mark over whether their one third status in the consortium will compensate for the loss."

Exton said the possibility of a Labour government establishing an "OffSky" regulator had not yet been factored into BSkyB's share price but added that market sentiment was short-term and riding high on hopes for the success of digital television.
"There's a perception that BSkyB will control the future of television in Europe."
